title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning Whether Service of Judicial Documents on Foreign Companies May Be Made on Their Representative Offices in China and Whether Service by Leaving May Be Applied

articles.content_en:
Fa Shi [2002] No. 15
Beijing Higher People's Court:
Your court's Jing Gao Fa [2001] No. 216, the "Request for Instructions on Whether Judicial Documents May Be Served on the Representative Office of a Foreign Company in China and Whether Substituted Service by Leaving the Documents at the Office May Apply" has been received. Upon study, the reply is as follows:
Article 1 of the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters (hereinafter referred to as the Hague Service Convention) provides: "The present Convention shall apply in all cases, in civil or commercial matters, where there is occasion to transmit a judicial or extrajudicial document for service abroad." Pursuant to Article 247 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), a People's Court may serve litigation documents on a party who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China in the manner prescribed by the international treaty concluded or jointly acceded to by the country where the person to be served has its domicile and the People's Republic of China; when the person to be served has a representative office within the territory of the People's Republic of China, this shall no longer fall within the circumstance of "occasions to transmit a judicial or extrajudicial document for service abroad" as stipulated in the Hague Service Convention. Therefore, a People's Court may serve litigation documents on the representative office established by the person to be served within the territory of the People's Republic of China in accordance with Article 247(5) of the Civil Procedure Law, without the need to effect service abroad under the Hague Service Convention.
Pursuant to Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law, when a People's Court serves litigation documents on the representative office of a foreign company in China, it may apply the method of substituted service by leaving the documents at the office.
This is our reply.
June 18, 2002
